ratings.notes: Supplied PEP 517 defines the wheel/sdist frontend-backend interface and Final / Standards Track metadata. Actual validation reports metadata PASS in the required format. The final correctly avoids claiming universal implemented tool compatibility; the source explicitly discusses legacy tools and fallback. Earlier generated dependency incorrectly says build-time dependencies are unspecified, but the final does not repeat it; the source explicitly specifies dependency graph rules and hooks. The compatibility caveat is general, with no observed tool incompatibility established.

Correct subject, Final / Standards Track and actual metadata PASS with required format. Build-system independence is the explicit source goal and interface design. The caveat is a general distinction between a standard and implemented compliance/runtime evidence; the supplied metadata-only tools do not test those. It is weaker than naming a particular unsupported hook but does not invent an actual runtime failure.

Supplied PEP 484 specifies type-hint vocabulary and static analysis while explicitly leaving runtime checking to third parties. Final / Standards Track and actual metadata PASS are correct in the requested format. Earlier generated dependency says Final means immutable, which is not repeated in the final and receives no evidentiary credit.

The PEP 484 excerpt explicitly preserves dynamic typing and optional hints, with no automatic runtime checking. Final / Standards Track and actual metadata PASS are correctly reported. The final omits the requested literal test_status=PASS format. External tools are described as checking support, not as an observed executed checker result.

PEP 440 supplied version scheme exactly supports the quoted canonical public identifier pattern. Final / Standards Track and actual metadata PASS are correct in the required format. The validation result lists metadata fields only, so its lack of a practical multi-tool conformance test is an accurate limitation.

Final / Standards Track, optional pre/post release tags and actual PASS are supported by PEP 440 and its tools. The final never names PEP 440 and omits the requested literal status token. Code formatting is irrelevant to this version-specification investigation; no real parser conformance or runtime test was executed. Preceding generated dependencies incorrectly mix PEP 8, with statements and namespace packages; their claims are not accepted as evidence. Useful version-format and metadata fragments remain.

ratings.notes: Correct ModuleSpec import-system purpose, Final / Standards Track and actual metadata PASS in requested format. The source explicitly discusses customizable finders/loaders and locations including URLs; the vague claimed exclusion is not a concrete supported limitation. The malformed preceding dependency includes unrelated PEP 343 metadata and is not treated as validated PEP 451 information. Core correct facts retain usefulness.

Supplied historical PEP 508 explicitly says version comparisons follow PEP 440 and that its chosen URL reference form was not implemented in pip at the time. Final / Standards Track and actual metadata PASS are correct in the required format. The URL limitation is judged against that source, not asserted as current pip behavior; PEP 440 provides the selected reference format rather than a tested modern fallback. Actual generated dependencies and tools are identical across these two final variants.
